prize_parts.citation: for the prediction of magic-angle flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in moire quantum materials

statement.case_for: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted, from a deliberately simple band-structure argument, that a specific twist angle quenches the bandwidth and drives the system into an interaction-dominated regime. The 2018 experiments of Jarillo-Herrero's group then found correlated insulators and superconductivity at that angle. A precise, falsifiable theoretical prediction followed by a clean experimental confirmation is the structure the prize rewards, and it is a pairing of exactly the kind of electronic-structure reasoning I work with. The results have been reproduced by many independent groups, and the platform now extends to other graphene multilayers and to transition-metal dichalcogenide moire systems. Eight years after the experiments the existence and importance of flat bands and correlated phases is secure, even though the pairing mechanism is not. The three credited names map cleanly onto one prediction and one experimental discovery, so no one has to be dropped to fit the three-person limit, which is not true of B006, B009 or B033. The citation deliberately rests on the flat-band prediction and the observation of correlated states, not on a superconducting mechanism.
statement.case_against: The field is young. The microscopic origin of the superconductivity and of several correlated phases is unsettled, and twist-angle disorder and sample dependence still limit how clean the phase diagram is. The prize would also bypass older and arguably more settled work such as optical lattice clocks (B046) and topological insulators (B038), which have been confirmed for much longer. Credit is not fully clean: earlier continuum-model work on twisted bilayers (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) and the experimental first authors (Cao, Fatemi and others) are outside the credited set, and I cannot verify the priority record from the supplied text alone.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp topological insulator work first, arguing that it is original, extensively confirmed over fifteen years in HgTe and in 3D materials by ARPES, and arguably overdue.
responses.response: I agree that B038 is scientifically at least as deep as B042 and better matured, and I rank it third myself. My difficulty is attribution rather than merit. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe realisation that Molenkamp observed, and the 3D route (Fu-Kane-Mele, Moore-Balents, Hsieh-Hasan) lies outside this entry, so a Kane-Mele-Molenkamp prize would tell an incomplete story that the committee would have to defend. There is also overlap with the 2016 topological-phases prize, which Mehlig himself notes. I therefore keep B038 as my first alternative rather than the preferred configuration, but I would not oppose it if colleagues find the credit chain acceptable.

responses.point: Lindroth places optical lattice clocks first as a clear, original idea with precision near 1e-18, a pending redefinition of the second and a clean two-laureate credit.
responses.response: I take the B046 case seriously and it has the strongest opening support among colleagues. The scientific quality is not in doubt, and a two-name credit is cleaner than my own. I still have two reservations. Lindroth herself lists whether the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-clock prize already cover much of the ground, and whether recognition should wait for the redefinition of the second. The magic-wavelength insight is a beautiful idea, but a good part of the later impact is accuracy records and applications that are still unfolding. I do not rank it above B042 for novelty and breadth of consequence, but I would not call it a mistake, and I list it as an alternative.

responses.point: Pearce ranks B046 first and B042 only seventh, on the grounds that the pairing mechanism in magic-angle graphene is unsettled and the field is still young, so recognition might be early.
responses.response: The pairing mechanism is a fair concern and I raise it myself, but I do not think the prize needs to rest on it. The flat-band prediction and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity are firmly established and reproduced across groups, and Olsson makes the same point that the citation can be limited to those. Timing is eight years after the experiments, which is not unusual for a strongly confirmed discovery with a large community behind it. What would change my view is evidence that the correlated phases are strongly sample-dependent in ways that undermine the reproducibility claim; I see no such evidence in the openings.

responses.point: Olsson ranks B042 first, as a precise and falsifiable prediction with decisive experiments, and says the superconducting mechanism should not carry the prize.
responses.response: I agree with the scope she proposes. The one place I would add care is credit: she notes that experimental credit is concentrated on one group while earlier twisted-graphene work exists, and I think the committee must be explicit that the citation covers the magic-angle prediction and its experimental discovery, not all moire physics. I also note that B042 and B038 are the two candidates where the theory-plus-experiment pairing is cleanest, which is a reason to keep both near the top.

responses.point: Danielsson places B042 sixth, accepting the originality of the prediction but suggesting the case may be premature relative to older candidates and noting that Cao and Fatemi and earlier theorists are not credited.
responses.response: I accept the credit caveat and have said it in my own case against. On prematurity, I would point out that the moire field has produced independent confirmations over several material families, including twisted TMD systems, which gives it a stability that a young field often lacks. I would be more worried about prematurity if the discovery rested on a single laboratory.

uncertainties: Whether the unsettled superconducting pairing mechanism should delay recognition, or can be set aside by a citation limited to flat bands and observed correlated states.
Whether earlier continuum-model work on twisted bilayers and the experimental co-first authors can be handled by wording the citation narrowly, since only three names are allowed.
How the committee should weigh the better-matured B046 and B038 against B042, given the strong opening support for B046 among colleagues.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile. My work on electronic-structure theory and two-dimensional materials at Uppsala is in a neighbouring area to B042, but no documented personal or institutional connection to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer is stated. I also chaired the 2025 prize committee, which matters for how I weigh B006 against its closeness to that prize rather than as a conflict.
